mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in GDPC1, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 YoY growth accelerates by > 2pp but SPX 60-day forward returns are negative, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5pp over 3 months signals a rapidly weakening labor market, which will pressure consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive, or Rank IC > -0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) declines by more than 2% YoY, it signals a supply-driven slowdown that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if accompanied by rising unemployment.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines > 2% YoY and UNRATE is rising, but SPX 60-day forward returns are positive, or Rank IC > -0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and rising, it signals a tightening monetary cycle that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, especially if accompanied by falling consumer spending.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising, and RSAFS is falling, but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive, or Rank IC > -0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Steadily rising housing starts (HOUST) over a 6-month period signal a strengthening housing market and consumer spending, which will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST rises steadily over 6 months but SPX 20-day forward returns are negative, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5pp over 3 months signals a rapidly tightening labor market, which will boost wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE declines > 0.5pp in 3 months but SPX 60-day forward returns are negative, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising by more than 3% YoY and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, it signals an inflationary environment that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, especially if accompanied by falling industrial production.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rising > 3% YoY and FEDFUNDS < 2%, and INDPRO is falling, but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive, or Rank IC > -0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) declines by more than 200,000 jobs over 3 months, it signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, especially if accompanied by falling retail sales.
failure_condition: PAYEMS declines > 200,000 over 3 months and RSAFS is falling, but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive, or Rank IC > -0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
